Differential split-sample test: calibrate in one climate, test in another

Source: R/splits.R
make_climate_contrast_folds.Rd

Klemes (1986, Hydrol. Sci. J. 31:13) proposed calibrating on climatically contrasting periods to test whether a model transfers to a changed climate – the closest historical check on using a model with climate projections. Water years after the warm-up are ranked by annual precipitation, annual mean temperature, and time. Each contrast trains on one extreme fraction of years and tests on the opposite extreme: 1 wet -> dry, 2 dry -> wet, 3 cool -> warm, 4 warm -> cool, 5 early -> late (calibrate on the first years, test on the most recent). Years in the middle are "unused". Process models still run the whole record; only scoring is restricted.

Usage

make_climate_contrast_folds(
  daily,
  frac = 1/3,
  warmup_years = 1,
  min_obs_frac = 0.8
)

Arguments

daily

Daily tibble with date, prcp_mm, tmean_c (and q_mm if min_obs_frac > 0).

frac

Fraction of scoreable water years in each extreme group.

warmup_years

Leading water years never scored.

min_obs_frac

Water years with less than this fraction of observed flow days are not ranked or scored.

Value

Long tibble: fold, contrast, date, wy, role ("train", "test", "warmup", "unused"), in the same layout as make_blocked_folds().
